title: harness-diet-score-guard (T3 ref): calculator spec + wiring history
desc: T3 reference tier of harness-diet-score-guard. The diet-score v2 calculator spec (bloat penalty weights), the wiring saga (dead-stub discovery, circular skill-currency deadlock, the ROOT misread-then-correction on how to raise a skill's coverage score), and the proto/wiring history that led to the live hard-block.
steps: DIET-SCORE v2 SPEC (Opus 2026-06-25): the original Get-WkClaudeMdDietScore was a born-stub (base 100, two no-op += 0 placeholders, never dropped below 90) so the <60 block never fired, and it was also nested inside an if-not-cheap-tier check so it skipped Haiku/codex delegations entirely. Real calculator design: base 100 minus weighted bloat penalties -- wksplit-400-lock line density (weight 25), stale-timestamp ratio (weight 20), duplicate skill-read 3-line clusters (weight 20), line count over 600 (weight 10), max contiguous non-header section length (weight 5) -- plus a REWARD for pointer density (skill-read lines / nonblank lines, weight 20, target over 30pct) and an optional bonus for the fraction of pointers a Haiku subagent actually read in the last 30 days. Guard wiring: fail-closed on a null score, an implausible-high cross-check (score>=80 but lines>300 is itself a defect signal), block under 60, warn 60-79, and an escape env var for emergencies.

IRONY + SOURCE FIX (2026-06-25): the wksplit-400-lock AUTO-REGISTRATION mechanism (which appends a per-file harness:skill block to CLAUDE.md whenever a large source file is read) had ITSELF bloated CLAUDE.md to about 78 percent of the file -- the split-your-source reminder became the single biggest bloat source, since it appended one block per file forever with no dedup. Healed by collapsing to one family wildcard block; the root fix (never appending a per-file block when a wildcard already covers it) was flagged as still needed at the source.

WIRING SAGA -- CIRCULAR DEADLOCK + MISREAD (2026-06-26): applying the verified calculator to the live guard file was blocked by a circular skill-currency lock (the file referenced a low-score skill, and the fix that would remove that reference was itself blocked by the same low-score skill). During this, a mistaken belief that the remediation was to add-step to raise a skill's score actually made things WORSE (steps do not count toward coverage score at all -- only id/title/desc/tags do), and this was later self-corrected: the real fix for a low-coverage skill is short good tags and a tight title/desc, never more steps.

LIVE HARD-BLOCK CONFIRMED (2026-07-01): the diet-score gate now genuinely hard-blocks Agent.cmd (the bash CLI wrapper) dispatches with rc=2 when CLAUDE.md's diet-score is under 60, printing the score and BLOATED verdict before the harness block. Observed specifically scoped to the Agent.cmd bash entry point -- the native in-IDE Agent tool did not trip this same gate in the same session. Escape when self-fixing is itself blocked: use the native Agent tool instead of Agent.cmd, or verify whether wkcodex.sh carries a separate exemption before assuming it works (a documented --file argument-parsing gap in wkcodex.sh means passing a brief file may silently no-op rather than actually dispatching).

SAFE DIET-HEAL TECHNIQUE -- WILDCARD BROADENING (2026-07-02, live-applied): the #1 duplicate-cluster bloat source in a study-lock-heavy CLAUDE.md is often the SAME 2-3 'floor' skills (e.g. a universal verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static / wksplit-cs-utility pair) repeated in dozens of per-file harness:skill blocks. SAFE FIX: find the EXISTING consolidated wildcard (union semantics -- a matched file gets the wildcard's skills PLUS its own file-specific lock), broaden its regex to cover more of the files currently repeating those skills individually (e.g. from a name-prefix-restricted pattern to a directory-scoped one like tools/**/*.ps1), then strip the now-redundant lines from each individual block that the broadened wildcard already covers. SAFETY: broadening a union wildcard is ALWAYS safe-direction (adds a requirement to more files, never removes one) -- the only risk is verifying the removed lines really are covered by the new wildcard scope before deleting them (check the block's file pattern actually matches the new wildcard regex). Live result: broadened tools/**/*.ps1 coverage, cut the verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static duplicate count from 31 occurrences to 19 (the remaining 19 are legitimately in .cmd/.sh/.yml/.py files outside the .ps1-only wildcard's scope -- a second wildcard for those file types would reduce further).

GROUND-TRUTH LIVE FORMULA (2026-07-02, corrects the v2 spec document above -- what actually SHIPPED is much simpler than the design doc described). Read directly from wkharness-guards-evidence.ps1 lines 75-109. Constants: LINE_BUDGET=200, BYTE_BUDGET_KB=12.0, PEN_PER_LINE=0.12, PEN_PER_KB=1.5, PEN_PER_BLOAT=0.30. Formula: lineOver=max(0,lineCount-200); linePen=lineOver*0.12. kbOver=max(0,byteKB-12.0); bytePen=kbOver*1.5. bloatLines=count of lines matching /^##\s*wksplit-400-lock/i OR /\(read on 20/ OR /\bauto:\s*\d+\s*lines/; bloatPen=bloatLines*0.30. score=100-linePen-bytePen-bloatPen (clamped 0-100). KEY INSIGHT: bytePen is ~12x more sensitive per unit than linePen (1.5 vs 0.12) -- there is NO duplicate-skill-cluster penalty, NO pointer-density reward, NO max-section-length penalty in the LIVE code (those were all v2-SPEC ideas that never shipped in this simpler form). PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: stripping trailing inline comments from lines (byte reduction with ZERO line-count change) is the highest-leverage, lowest-risk diet-heal lever -- far more effective per edit than deduplicating skill-read lines (which the live formula does not penalize at all). Live-verified: wkappbot-kih's CLAUDE.md went 42(36151B/364L) -> 47(32557B, after removing structural duplicates, which helped only via incidental byte/line reduction, NOT duplicate-detection) -> 62(27050B/337L, after aggressive comment-stripping and prose condensation) across 3 rounds. WORKFLOW FOR NEXT TIME: read the LIVE calculator source FIRST (do not trust a spec/design skill without cross-checking against shipped code), compute current score by hand from wc -l / wc -c, then trim BYTES first (comments, verbose prose) before worrying about line count or structural dedup.
